column6: The back-translation uses the term 'inclination' instead of 'minded,' but both phrases convey the same theological concept of the conflict between the flesh and the Spirit, maintaining the original meaning without altering the doctrinal implications.
column7: > **<u>Romans 8:6-8</u>** (NKJV)\\\\n>\\\\n> For to be carnally minded is death, but to be spiritually minded is life and peace.\\\\n>\\\\n> Because the carnal mind is enmity against God; for it is not subject to the law of God, nor indeed can be.\\\\n>\\\\n> So then, those who are in the flesh cannot please God.\\\\n>
column8: > **<u>Romans 8:6-8</u>** (NKJV)\\\\n>\\\\n> For the inclination of the flesh is death, but the inclination of the Spirit is life and peace.\\\\n>\\\\n> Because the inclination of the flesh is enmity against God; for it is not subject to the law of God, nor indeed can it be.\\\\n>\\\\n> So then, those who are in the flesh cannot please God.\\\\n>
